request.state:
Target: Apple (AAPL). Apple develops and sells personal computing devices including iPhone, Mac and iPad, with operating systems and digital services.

Focal announcement: App Store stopped more than $2 billion in fraudulent transactions in 2022.

Decision cutoff: 2023-05-16T23:59:59-04:00. Only information available before this cutoff is admissible.

Source: App Store stopped more than $2 billion in fraudulent transactions in 2022. Published: 2023-05-16. URL: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2023/05/app-store-stopped-more-than-2-billion-in-fraudulent-transactions-in-2022.

Condensed source facts; other details are omitted: The App Store launched in 2008 with the mission of accomplishing two important objectives: to establish a reliable and secure platform for users to safely discover and download apps, and to provide developers with an exciting opportunity to showcase their ideas and grow their business. Today, Apple announced that in 2022, the App Store prevented over $2 billion in potentially fraudulent transactions, and rejected nearly 1.7 million app submissions for failing to meet the App Store’s high standards for privacy, security, and content. Apple detected and blocked more than 147 million fraudulent ratings and reviews from the App Store last year. Apple blocked a record $2 billion in fraudulent transactions in 2022, banning 714,000 fraudulent accounts from transacting again. In total, Apple blocked $2.09 billion in fraudulent transactions on the App Store in 2022.

The exact historical text version is unverified. This is an incomplete source-based reconstruction.

Expectations: No point-in-time analyst consensus or market-implied expectation is available.

No company-wide comparable financial baselines or incremental magnitude inputs were supplied. Do not infer that a large headline amount is material to the target.

The stock had no net price change over the latest completed session.

The stock showed a very small past rise over the recent trading week, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The stock showed a modest past rise over the recent trading month, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The stock's recent daily variability was moderate. Variability describes the size of ordinary fluctuations, not their future direction.

The broad market (SPY) showed a substantial past decline over the latest completed session, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The broad market (SPY) showed a very small past decline over the recent trading week, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The broad market (SPY) showed a very small past decline over the recent trading month, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The broad market (SPY)'s recent daily variability was relatively subdued. Variability describes the size of ordinary fluctuations, not their future direction.

Over the recent trading week, the stock showed very small outperformance relative to the broad market.

Over the recent trading month, the stock showed modest outperformance relative to the broad market.

The stock and broad market moved in opposite directions over the recent week, so their historical directional signals conflict.

These are coarse descriptions computed from observed historical inputs. Strong past movement or relative strength is not evidence that the next return must continue or reverse.

The previously fitted market-only reference model favored an upward return beyond the neutral band. Its leading outcome was only slightly favored. It still assigned meaningful possibility to a return inside the narrow neutral band and a downward return beyond the neutral band. This is a training-only model forecast, not an observed outcome or independent news evidence.

The neutral return band's half-width is narrower than the code-computed ordinary five-session variability scale. An irrelevant article does not eliminate ordinary price movement; this is not a calculated class probability.

Forecast target: entry is the first regular-session open after the cutoff; exit is the fifth session close, counting entry as session one. Raw return above +1% is up; within inclusive -1% to +1% is flat; below -1% is down. The initial pre-entry reaction is outside this target.

Do not invent analyst consensus, incremental target sales, new corporate cash payments, or an already-priced news reaction.
